caseno: Death Reference No.98 of 2004 with Criminal Appeal No. 4314 of 2004.
lawyer:
Md Shamsul Haque, Deputy Attorney-General with Israt Jahan, Assistant Attorney-General ------ For the State. 
Syed Mizanur Rahman, Advocate ------ For the Appellant.
parties:
State ------ Petitioner
vs
Mirajul Sheikh ------ Appellant
full_judgment:
Md Anwarul Haque J: This Criminal Appeal, at the instance of the condemned prisoner Md Mirajul Sheikh son of Abdul Sheikh, is directed against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence of death, passed by the learned Judge of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Faridpur on 6-7-2004 in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal Case No. 67 of 2003 arising out of GR Case No. 437 of 2002 corresponding to Kotwali PS Case No. 25 dated 23-10-2002 punishable under section 11(ka)/4(1) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. 

 2. At the same time the Death Reference Case No. 98 of 2004 submitted by the learned Judge of the Tribunal under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure read with section 29 of the Nori4Shishtt Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 for confirmation of sentence of death awarded by him to the condemned-prisoner is also taken up together for hearing and disposal since these two matters are the product of the same judgment. 

 3. Prosecution case as unfolded, in short, is as follows: 

 5. Thereafter on the following morning at about 10-20 AM PW 1, brother of the deceased, Saidur Rahman Akhter lodged the ejahar Exhibit 1. where a case punishable under section. 11(ka)/30 was recorded implicating 3 accused-persons. namely Md Mirajul Sheikh son of Md  Abdul Sheikh, Abdul Alim son of Fazar Ali, Jahanara Begum wife of Sheikh Sohrab in the list of the accused. Recording this Case Officer-in-Charge, Kotwali. PS Faridpur, PW 6 filled up the FIR forth EXhibit 4 and handed over it to Sub-Inspector Anowar Hossain, PW 7 for investigation. 

 6. During the course of investigation the investigating officer visited the place of occurrence, prepared the inquest report Exhibit 7 and sent it to the morgue for autopsy. He also prepared the sketch map with index Exhibits 5 and 6 respectively and recorded the statement of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, seized alamat under seizure list Exhibit 8, collected postmortem report Exhibit 7 and produced the principal accused. Mirajul Sheikh before the learned Magistrate to record his confessional statement Exhibit 2 and ultimately handed over the case-dairy to the officer-in-charge of the police station 14-11-2002 before his departure for departmental training. Thereafter, PW 8, Sub-Inspector Abul Kalam Azad, examined the evidence, collected by PW 7 Sub-Inspector Md Anowar Hossain, and submitted the report with a recommendation to stand trial of those three accused-persons, named in the FIR Exhibit 1. 

 8. During the course Of trial prosecution has produced as many as 8 witnesses including PW 4, Dr Ajoy Kumar Sarker who conducted the post mortem examination on the body of the deceased and PW 7 Sub-Inspector Md Anowar Hossain and PW 8 Sub-Inspector Abul Kalam Azad investigating officer of this case. However, the defence case as it transpires from the trend of cross-examination and suggestion put to the PWs is that they have been falsely implicated in the case out of enmity when the deceased succumbed to her burn injury, which was accidental in nature. 

 9. However considering the evidence on record, adduced by the prosecution and the defence version, transmitted during cross-examination, the learned Judge of the Tribunal has found the accused guilty of the offence punishable under section 4(1)/11 (ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and awarded death penalty to him with an observation that it is a pure case of custodial death of the deceased where husband, the condemned-prisoner has not given any satisfactory explanation about the cause of death and the post-mortem report Exhibit 3 also stands for injury which was ante mortem and homicidal in nature. Beside, such evidence the learned Judge of the Tribunal has also relied upon the confessional statement of the accused Exhibit 7 where he has depicted the lucid picture of the incident and his over tact in the commission of the offence of murder of his wife, the deceased, Shefali. 

 11. Moreover, in the case of an offence punishable under section 4(1) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 the death must be caused with the help of combustible, corrosive or poisonous substance, otherwise judge of the tribunal constituted by section 26 of the said law bears no authority to try those accused persons taking cognizance for the commission of the said offence. 

 12. At the same time no husband can be brought within the mischief of section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 unless the demand of dowry is proved where, of course, the cause of death by the husband is immaterial. In the instant case neither the demand of dowry has been proved nor use of combustible substance for causing ante mortem burn injury has been proved with the help of the evidence or symptom available on the person of the deceased, so Court must not go to find the accused guilty of the offence punish: able under section (1)/11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 only on the plea of custodial death of the wife. He goes to argue that if death is found to have been caused otherwise the husband or other inmates of the house may be tried under general law-of the country but not Under this special law. So, the judgment of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Adalat has got no scope of jurisdiction to find the accused guilty of the Offence of death of the wife without" fulfilling' the conditions as required under section 4(1) or 11(ka) of 'the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000: Moreover, the trial has not been commenced within the statutory period as prescribed under section 31 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 which has been incorporated in the Act by way of amendment (Act 30 of 2003). The learned Advocate further submits that the examination of the condemned-prisoner under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure since has not also been properly made which is sufficient enough to vitiate the trial. In fine, the learned advocate for the appellant-condemned-prisoner has also prayed for commutation of sentence since the condemned-prisoner is too young to be hanged because he had enough opportunity to be influenced by other co-accused-persons who has been acquitted for want of legal evidence. In support of his contention the learned Advocate for the condemned-prisoner has referred .a decision of  a case Mojibur Rahman Gazi vs State reported in 46 DLR 423 and a case State vs Shamim @ Shamim Sikder  reported in 53 DLR 339 where their Lordships have observed that awarding death sentence to a condemned-prisoner aged about of 20-22 years living in death cell for a period of more than 3 years, is sufficient to constitute extenuating circumstances in order to commute death sentence to imprisonment for life since the death sentence with be too harsh to the accused having such youth age. 

 13. On the other hand Mr Md Shamsul Haque the learned Deputy Attorney-General has supported the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence, under reference, passed by the learned Judge of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, alleging inter alia that the post-mortem report Exhibit 3 is enough to prove the cause of death of the deceased as burn injuries, mentioned therein Exhibit 3 which was ante mortem and homicidal in nature. So, there cannot be any doubt about the use of combustible substance to cause the death of the deceased at such the learned Judge of the Tribunal has committed no error in convicting the accused under section 4(1)/11 (ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000, More so, the learned Deputy has Attorney-General has emphatically argued that since the demand of dowry has also been duly proved with the help of unimpeachable evidence of PW 1 Md Saidur Rahman Akhter and PW 2 Nasim Sheikh and custodial death of the newly wedded wife has also been admitted by the condemned-prisoner in his confessional statement Exhibit 7 which has neither been retracted in time nor a case of demand of dowry resulting to the death of the wife has been denied by the husband, so use of combustible, corrosive or poisonous substance to cause death has become immaterial. Even the case as has been proved by the prosecution with the help of PW 1 & 2 is sufficient enough to bring the case within the scope of section 11(ka) of the said Ain, 2000 where only ante-mortem injury to cause homicidal death is required. It is also argued that the application of section 4(1) of the said Ain has become redundant one; since the case as proved by the prosecution can easily be brought under section 11(ka) of the said Ain. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that when the newly wedded wife was in the custody of the accused at the time of commission of the offence of murder in pursuance of demand of dowry the duty of the Court to secure the punishment of the husband under section 11(ka) of the said AM which has been specially promulgated for husband community as a deterrent punishment. In support of his contention the learned Deputy Attorney-General has referred a decision of a case the State vs Shafiqul Islam reported in 43 DLR (AD) 92 where their Lord-ships have positively observed that in wife-killing case prosecution is to depend upon the circumstantial evidence because collection of ocular evidence is quite impossible when wife is killed in the custody of the husband in the later husband's house. In the instant case there is no denial of killing of the wife in the custody of the husband, condemned-prisoner and no satisfactory explanation has also been given by the husband condemned-prisoner, about the cause of death of his wife rather the condemned-prisoner himself has corroborated the case of the prosecution in his inculpatory confessional statement, recorded under section 164 of the CrPC Exhibit 2 which is true and voluntary, as asserted by the recording Magistrate PW 3, Md Mofizul Islam. In such circumstances relying upon the evidence of PW 1 Md Saidur Rahman Akhter and PW 2 Nasim Sheikh who have not even before controverted by the accused in any way and their evidence relating to demand of dowry remains unchallenged. As such the case has been rightly brought within the mischief of section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirja tan Daman Ain, 2000 where use of combustible, corrosive or poisons substance is not, at all, required. So, the learned Judge of the Tribunal has rightly found the accused guilty for committing the offence punishable under section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 which needs no interference. 

 14. Moreover, the learned Deputy Attorney-General has also argued that though the confessional statement of the condemned-prisoner, recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not found to have been brought to the notice of the accused at the time of examination under section 342 of the Code of criminal Procedure in a black and white but factually it was so done since he made a reply retracting the confessional statement done by him alleging that it was neither voluntary nor true. So, he has not been prejudiced in any way as such, no benefit can be given to him as argued by the learned Advocate of the condemned-prisoner. In fact, the accused, husband of the deceased, took an opportunity for the first time to retract his confessional statement at the time of examination under section 342 of the CrPC. So, only the alleged non-mentioning the confessional statement at the time of examination of the accused has caused no mischief to him since in the same occasion he himself mentioned the existence of such confessional statement in order to retract if for the first time. In support of this contention the learned Deputy Attorney-General has referred a decision of a case State vs Nurul Hoque reported in 45 DLR 306 where their Lordships have positively observed that the belated retraction at the end of trial would be of no value. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has further argued that the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant so far it relates to commutation of sentence is of no substance because the punishment for committing the offence punishable under section 11(ka) is only death. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that prosecution preserves the right to produce the witnesses as per his requirement which cannot be regulated by the accused-person. In the instant case where the charge is found to have been proved by inculpatory confessional statement of the accused and the unimpeachable evidence of PW 1, 2, 3 and other medical officer PW 4 Dr Ajoy Kumar Sarker, the question of production of other local witnesses in a wife-killing case is immaterial. 

 17. PW 2 Nasim Sheikh, father of the deceased has also corroborated the case of the prosecution so far it relates to demand of dowry in a harmonious voice. He has categorically stated that— 

 19. PW 2 Nasim Sheikh and father of the deceased has proved the demand of dowry beyond any shadow of doubt in a harmonious voice with the PW 1 which has not even been denied by the accused by putting such suggestion to them. So, we find it needless to discuss more in order to say that the death has caused due to the failure, to fulfill the demand to dowry which is to be easily brought within the mischief of section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan- Daman Ain, 2000 which runs as follows: 

 24. PW 7 Sub-Inspector Anowar Hossain, being investigating officer, visited the place of occurrence and prepared sketch map with index Exhibit 5 and 6 respectively and also prepared inquest report Exhibit 7 on 23-10-2002 and seized alamat under seizure list Exhibit 8 and securing the arrest of the accused he produced him before the learned Magistrate to record the confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, Exhibit 7. Thereafter on 14-11-2002 he handed over the case docket to the then Officer-in-charge before his departure to attend training course outside Dhaka. During cross-examination he has categorically asserted that he saw the injury on the body of the deceased but he did not seize the wearing cloths of the deceased under seizure list. 

 25. PW 8 Sub-Inspector Abul Kalam Azad, also being entrusted to investigate into the case, examined all the evidence recorded by PW 7 Sub-Inspector Anowar Hossain under 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and ultimately submitted charge sheet on 20-2-2003 with a recommendation to stand trial of the accused-person for committing the offence, referred to above. During cross-examination no specific suggestion has been given in order to extort benefit in the name of the contradiction with the statement recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 26. On close examination of the evidence discussed above as well as the confessional statement Exhibit 7, given by the condemned prisoner of the case, implicating him in the offence of the commission of the murder of his wife in his custody is also examined here meticulously which runs as follows: 

 29. On analytical reading of the catena of decisions of our Apex Court referred to above, it is found that it is the husband who will explain the plausible reason or cause of death of wife in his custody. But in the instant case no such explanation has been given by the husband exculpating him in the offence of commission of murder rather has given confessional statement inculpating him in the offence of murder. 

 30. It is true that such crime against newly wedded women are generally committed with-in the four wall of a house maintaining secrecy there. Independent eye-witnesses or other direct evidence is scarcely available to the prosecution. In such circumstance inculcator confessional statement Exhibit 7 which has not been denied is enough to find the accused guilty of the offence punishable under section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 since demand of dowry as proved by the prosecution has not even been denied by the accused husband. In fact, the nature of burn injuries as found on the body of the deceased especially on the face, has been shown in order to screen out the evidence of cause of death which has been asserted by the accused-person in his confessional statement Exhibit 7. Moreover pouring kerosene on the person of the deceased if the accused causes fire by a matchstick certainly her wearing apparel like blouse cannot remain with its own colour and shape causing burn injuries on her chest. So, we find no scope to bring the case under section 4(1) of the said AM since use of combustible substance like kerosene has not been duly proved though custodial death has been proved beyond any shadow of doubt. 

 33. In the instant case there is no doubt about the custodial death of the wife where husband is to be considered main perpetrator of the crime. Importing name of another person in the commission of the offence the condemned-prisoner has made the confessional statement which is of no use since no other evidence is available against other accused-person who has already been acquitted by the Court below and no appeal has also been preferred by the prosecution. In this circumstances the confessional statement so far it relates to the maker only is to be considered along with other circumstantial evidence like the custodial death of the wife and the apprehension of the accused by the local people immediately after the occurrence and the confessional statement made by the accused husband within two days from the date of occurrence before the learned Magistrate, 1st Class on 24-10-2002. So, we find no way but to say that the accused being husband is fully responsible for the cause of death of his wife and his offence is to be brought only within, the mischief of section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 since such offence has been committed when wife failed to fulfill the demand of dowry which we have already decided with the help of PW 1 and PW 2 because both of them are found to be credible witnesses and the testimony inspires confidence which has not also been challenged. 

 34. So to the case in hand and facts found established, the section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000, only could be held to be attracted where use of combustible instance to cause death is immaterial. It only demands custodial death of husband having injury which is ante mortem and homicidal in nature in demand of dowry. 

 37. However, since we have already decided that the offence as has been proved comes within the mischief of section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 which prescribes only sentence of death as such, there is no scope of commutation of sentence in the form of life imprisonment even on any extenuating circumstance as alleged by the learned Advocate of the accused. The law is so stringent where the motive, intention or any extenuating circumstances will not go to regulate the punishment of the accused in any way and the youth age is of no consideration because only punishment prescribed by the law in case of murder of the wife for demand of dowry is death.
